cases.description: VS Code Pseudoterminal and provider contract methods are host-invoked callbacks, while unrelated methods on the same classes remain dead code.
TypeScript package entrypoints and imports should keep live exports reachable while stale TS and JS exports are reported.
Static namespace member reads and stable aliases retain selected exports without crediting unrelated or shadowed members.
Escaped namespaces and dynamic member keys keep all their exports while an unrelated internal helper remains unused.

Literal module namespace key enumeration follows resolved wildcard bindings even when generated package outputs are unavailable; private helpers remain unused.
A closed application reads compact through two namespace exports; expanded has no consumer. A native-valid tagged template must not make the source scope incomplete or disable exact export demand.
Escaping namespace preserves exported service functions; declared package API preserves renderer functions; private uncalled helpers remain dead in both providers.
With tsconfig jsx: react, JSX reads the React binding; a React import in a file without JSX is still unused.
With tsconfig jsx: react-jsx the compiler imports the runtime itself, so an unread React import is unused.
A @jsx pragma makes JSX read the named factory in that file only.
tsconfig jsxFactory names the binding JSX reads; React is unused under a custom factory.
A type namespace import used as the root of a qualified type name is read; unnamed type imports are unused.
Default values of destructured bindings and parameters read the import or constant they name.
Methods of a class that extends a dependency's class can be overrides the dependency calls; methods of base-less and project-base classes are judged normally.
A method called through an instance inside a declaration of the same name is used; a local variable that only shares a method's name is not a call.
Storybook loads its named .storybook config files; other files there and orphans need an importer.
Without a Storybook dependency or script, a .storybook file is an ordinary unused file.
karma.conf and wdio.conf in a package that uses the runner are loaded by it; WebdriverIO reads only the exported config.
A karma.conf.js in a package that neither depends on nor runs Karma is unused.
Path strings in a tool configuration file load the files they name; comments, prose and path strings in ordinary modules do not.
A tsconfig include entry that names one file is a compilation root; globs, excludes and unlisted files are not.
path.join/path.resolve from node:path with literal segments name the file they build; comments, Array.join and local lookalikes do not.
A runtime command built in a template literal runs the script it names; prose and non-command joins do not.
A runtime command in a Markdown code block or code span is a run instruction; prose, links and non-runtime commands are mentions.
package.json files entries that name one file and path values of custom keys load that file; folder entries, descriptions and ignore lists do not.
In a React Native project an import loads every platform sibling of its target; platform files nobody imports stay unused.
Without React Native or Expo, scale.web.ts is an ordinary module that needs its own importer.
An `export { X } from` statement re-exports from the module and does not read a local import of X; a local `export { X }` does.
A default export re-exported by name from the package entry is public API.
Direct HTML script references preserve exact paths while ordinary and malformed comments do not load scripts.
Legacy IE conditional HTML script references preserve the exact asset without treating ordinary or malformed comments as loads.
Legacy IE conditional HTML script references support the native Jinja safe filter on simple literal paths while comments and wrong paths remain unused.
Imported aliases in a closed private package consume individual enum members.
